headline_marked: 12 killed, 50 injured as [[Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport]]
headline: 12 killed, 50 injured as Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport
summary: King Khalid International Airport operations are suspended following a deadly blast claimed by the Iran-backed Houthi group.
details: At least 12 people were killed and 50 others injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The Iran-backed Houthi armed group from Yemen has claimed responsibility for the blast.

Saudi civil aviation authorities have temporarily suspended airport operations to assess the extent of the damage. Biman Bangladesh Airlines has also suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice.

Houthi official Mohammed al-Bukhaiti stated the attack was a response to Saudi airstrikes on civilian infrastructure in Yemen. He claimed the operation was intended to show that civilian facilities should be protected globally.

The attack comes amid escalating tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, following a period of instability in the region since February. Western embassies, including the US, have advised citizens to avoid the area.

US President Donald Trump acknowledged the attack and stated that a decision regarding potential US intervention would be made. The US had previously conducted bombing campaigns against the Houthis last year.
This incident threatens Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's vision to transform Riyadh into a global hub for travel and business, potentially disrupting upcoming international events.
caption:

headline_marked: Over 2,000 [[detained in Delhi over disputed voter rolls]]
headline: Over 2,000 detained in Delhi over disputed voter rolls
summary: Security forces locked down the capital to prevent protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
details: Indian police detained more than 2,000 protesters in Delhi and approximately 400 in Mumbai on Saturday, as security forces locked down parts of the capital to prevent a rally.
The demonstrations, organized by the Cockroach movement, targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over revisions to voter lists that critics claim disproportionately benefit the ruling BJP.
Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and other senior leaders upon their arrival in Delhi, while security forces sealed off the Jantar Mantar area.
The crackdown included the detention of opposition lawmakers and former chief ministers, including Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, and Pinarayi Vijayan.
Security forces established checkpoints on major roads, suspended mobile internet in the central business district, and shut down dozens of metro stations and markets.
The unrest follows reports that two election commissioners questioned the removal of roughly 130 million entries from the voter lists.
While the BJP denies any wrongdoing and attributes electoral success to popularity, opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi have vowed to continue their protests.
caption:
Over 2,000 people detained and the capital locked down. Why is India's voter list causing such unrest?

Indian police detained more than 2,000 protesters in Delhi and approximately 400 in Mumbai on Saturday, as security forces locked down parts of the capital to prevent a rally.

The demonstrations, organized by the Cockroach movement, targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over revisions to voter lists that critics claim disproportionately benefit the ruling BJP.

Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and other senior leaders upon their arrival in Delhi, while security forces sealed off the Jantar Mantar area.

The crackdown included the detention of opposition lawmakers and former chief ministers, including Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, and Pinarayi Vijayan.

Security forces established checkpoints on major roads, suspended mobile internet in the central business district, and shut down dozens of metro stations and markets.

The unrest follows reports that two election commissioners questioned the removal of roughly 130 million entries from the voter lists.

While the BJP denies any wrongdoing and attributes electoral success to popularity, opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi have vowed to continue their protests.
